$comment: Every public claim and what proves it. A claim's proof is a file in this repository (and, optionally, text that file must contain). scripts/check-claims.mjs fails the build when a proof is missing, and when a page cites a claim that is not here. status: released (in the published release), next (built and tested, not yet published); none is "next" while a release is current.

claims.text: A model call never runs inside a workflow transaction; its result enters process state only through an engine command that validates it.
The engine checks every agent answer against its declared output schema, result variable and confidence threshold, and routes a weak or malformed answer to a declared path, usually a person.
Conditions and decision tables are sandboxed expressions evaluated inside the transaction; they cannot reach the JVM and fail loudly instead of guessing.

PostgreSQL and RustFS, both self-hosted, are the only required infrastructure: PostgreSQL holds process state and the metadata of task files, RustFS their contents; schema upgrades from every supported prior version are tested on PostgreSQL.
An agent's write to an outside system can require a person's approval of the exact call, and a crash never repeats an approved write.
A process can start a governed child process, and an agent can propose to; an engine kill mid-child neither duplicates nor orphans it.
Every agent step leaves an auditable record (model, tokens, cost, timings, actors) in the same store as the process state, with payloads encrypted and cleared after a retention period.
The engine is open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0, and the worker SDK is Apache-2.0.
The Insight loop notices when people keep overruling an agent, when its confidence drifts, or when it becomes expensive, and says which step it concerns.
A proposed change can be replayed on recorded cases before anyone approves it, and a policy can require it. A replay is evidence of what would have changed, not a verdict.
A process can be returned to an earlier version with one audited action; instances already running are not touched.
A natural-language refinement is applied as a short list of operations the engine validates, and is refused rather than faked when no model is available.
A process can run a governed child per item of a list, with a hard bound on items and on how many run at once; one failing item does not stop the others.

The running platform never contacts Abada. The Linux and macOS installer sends one anonymous report when it finishes, limited to a fixed list of fields, with only country and region derived server-side and no IP address stored; it can be switched off with ABADA_USAGE_PING=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

proof.contains: refuses anything that is not on the list
